title: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
statement: For a contiguous block of elements of the integer array `nums`, add its elements together and take the absolute value of that total; call the result the block's absolute sum. The block may also be empty, in which case its absolute sum is `0`. Return the greatest absolute sum over every such block of `nums`.
notes:
## Intuition

The absolute value of a total is large either when the total is very positive or when it is very negative. So the answer is simply the larger of two classic questions: the biggest subarray sum and the smallest subarray sum (taken as a magnitude). Checking all O(n²) blocks works, but Kadane's dynamic programming answers both questions in one pass: the best sum of a block ending at index `i` either starts fresh at `nums[i]` or extends the best block ending at `i - 1`.

## Approach

1. Keep `maxEnding` (largest sum of a block ending here) and `minEnding` (smallest such sum), both `0`, and `best = 0` for the empty block.
2. For each `num`, set `maxEnding` to the larger of `num` alone and `maxEnding + num`.
3. Set `minEnding` to the smaller of `num` alone and `minEnding + num`.
4. Update `best` with `maxEnding` and `-minEnding`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `nums = [1, -3, 2, 3, -4]`:

| num | maxEnding | minEnding | best |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| -3 | -2 | -3 | 3 |
| 2 | 2 | -1 | 3 |
| 3 | 5 | 3 | 5 |
| -4 | 1 | -4 | 5 |

The block `[2, 3]` gives the answer `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1): three running numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Running only the maximum-sum Kadane misses answers like `[-2, -7]`, whose best block is negative.
- Taking `Math.abs` of each element first is wrong: signs inside a block cancel.
- The empty block makes the answer at least `0`, so start `best` at `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `maxEnding` | largest sum of a block that ends at the current element |
| `minEnding` | smallest sum of a block that ends at the current element |
| `best` | largest absolute sum found so far |
| `num` | the current element |

narration.2: maxEnding is the largest total of a block ending at the current element.
narration.3: minEnding is the smallest total of a block ending at the current element.
narration.4: The empty block has absolute sum 0, so the answer starts there.
narration.5: Scan the array once, extending blocks one element at a time.
narration.6: Either start a new block at num or extend the best block that ended just before.
narration.7: The same choice, but keeping the most negative total.
narration.8: A big positive total or a big negative total both give a big absolute sum.
narration.10: best now holds the largest absolute sum of any block.
